Addition and Subtraction of Functions

CurvesAlgebra
Game: Two curves, black f and green g, are added or subtracted point by point to make a third curve. Change f and g and watch the new curve follow.
How to play: Drag the black or green curve up or down anywhere along it. Choose f + g (blue) or f − g (red), and slide the marker to compare the heights.

fgf + g

Look for the math

Adding or subtracting two functions is done one input at a time: take the height of each graph at the same x and add or subtract them.

Point by point

(f + g)(x) = f(x) + g(x) and (f − g)(x) = f(x) − g(x). At the marker you can read off the three heights. The test checked these equalities at thousands of random places on randomly bent graphs.

What to look for

The difference is zero exactly where the graphs of f and g cross: the red curve touches the middle line there (the test finds each sign change and checks that f and g meet). Where g is zero the sum and difference both equal f. If g equals f, the difference is the flat line 0 and the sum is the double of f. And (f + g) − g = f: subtracting undoes adding.

A fact hidden in the picture

The curves are cubic splines: smooth curves through eleven points whose heights you drag. The blue curve is not computed separately. It is the cubic spline through the sums of the heights of the points of f and g, because building a spline from the heights is a linear operation. The test checks this on 300 random pairs of curves.

Make g exactly follow f. What happens to the red curve? Then flip g upside down and compare the red and blue curves.
